page: Amazon Web Services m5zn.3xlarge is a high-frequency general purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8252C processor running on the x86_64 architecture with a maximum clock frequency of 4.5 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 12 dedicated virtual CPUs across 6 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at 2 threads per core. System memory totals 48.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, providing a standard general-purpose allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

The platform includes no integrated local instance storage and operates without dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes for persistent and ephemeral data. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 15 Gbps. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512, and AES, supporting vectorized computing and cryptographic operations directly on the CPU cores.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the advantages of high clock speeds, showing strong single-threaded throughput in gzip compression reaching 31.64 GB/sec. General multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and Redis SET throughput (14.22 million operations per second) place within average industry thresholds for 12-thread instances. Large-scale LLM prompt processing shows lower efficiency on 7B parameter models due to the absence of dedicated matrix acceleration. The m5zn.3xlarge is well positioned for latency-sensitive applications requiring elevated per-core compute speeds, such as gaming dedicated servers, CI/CD compilation, financial simulations, and enterprise application backends.
description: Amazon Web Services m5zn.3xlarge is a high-frequency general purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an Intel Xeon 8252C processor operating at 4.5 GHz. Configured on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores and 48.0 GB of DDR4 RAM at 3 GHz, preserving a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance features no local storage and no GPU accelerators, routing I/O through network-attached storage alongside a 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate solid execution across standard computing profiles, highlighted by strong single-threaded throughput in compression tests. Balancing dedicated high-frequency cores against network-attached storage architectures, m5zn.3xlarge provides efficient throughput for latency-sensitive tasks, CI/CD compilation workloads, game server backends, and moderate relational database hosting.
